learnerOutcome: Configure and verify a router-local endpoint, distinguish static discard and reject next hops in the routing table, and demonstrate how ordered routing-policy terms admit one contributor and exclude another without removing the component routes.
observableOutcomes: lo0.0 reports service address 192.0.2.2/32, its local route exists in inet.0, and router-originated ping to 192.0.2.2 succeeds.
inet.0 reports active Static route 172.16.10.0/24 with a discard next hop.
inet.0 reports active Static route 172.17.10.0/24 with a reject next hop.
inet.0 reports active Aggregate route 172.16.0.0/16 after the exact approved static contributor is admitted.
inet.0 contains no route for aggregate destination 172.17.0.0/16 after passive retention is removed and the unwanted contributor is rejected.
Both component Static routes and the service endpoint remain usable after contributor policy takes effect.
Both distinct self-linked data ports report administrative and operational up throughout the exercise.
rationale: This practices addressing, static routing, and policy on one appliance. A same-router wire provides measured ordinary appliance readiness while local operational state carries the taught outcomes. Aggregate contribution supplies a real local policy effect, without route advertisement or transit claims. Every stage check fails at original start/reset and stays true at final handover. The engineer must establish the passive-summary scaffold and accepted/rejected policy effects with native tools and snapshots before an accepted submission.
scenario: You are preparing one ordinary router for a small local routing exercise. Two data ports are joined by a same-router wire so the appliance starts with healthy ports; no second node or logical system is present. A diagnostic loopback endpoint already works, but a second endpoint and two planned routes are missing. An unwanted summary is retained without contributors; your final policy must make only the approved summary active while keeping both component routes.

stageSketch.achieves: Done when 192.0.2.2/32 appears on lo0.0, its local route is present in inet.0, and r1 can ping that address while the diagnostic endpoint remains reachable.
stageSketch.title: Establish the local service endpoint

stageSketch.achieves: Done when inet.0 contains active Static routes for 172.16.10.0/24 with a discard next hop and 172.17.10.0/24 with a reject next hop, and the service endpoint still works.
stageSketch.title: Represent the two planned networks

stageSketch.achieves: Done when contributor policy makes 172.16.0.0/16 an active Aggregate route, 172.17.0.0/16 is absent, both component Static routes remain active, and the service endpoint still works.
stageSketch.title: Admit only the approved contributor

startStateSketch: One initialized vJunos-router r1 has one same-router link between two distinct host-assigned data ports, already up/up with no addressing required by the exercises; there are no other nodes or logical systems. The wired ports and diagnostic endpoint 192.0.2.1/32 on lo0.0 remain healthy throughout. Service endpoint 192.0.2.2/32, static routes 172.16.10.0/24 and 172.17.10.0/24, and approved summary 172.16.0.0/16 are absent. Unwanted aggregate summary 172.17.0.0/16 is retained with its passive property, so a check requiring that summary to be absent fails at the original start.
title: Local Addressing, Static Routes, and Contributor Policy
